title: Historical Appendix: The Fall of Jerusalem

questions.question: How old was Zedekiah when he became king, and how long did he reign in Jerusalem?
options: Twenty-one years old / reigned eleven years
Eight years old / reigned thirty-one years
Twenty-five years old / reigned sixteen years
Thirty years old / reigned forty years
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-one years old / reigned eleven years
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:1 (ESV): "Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem."

questions.question: What did Zedekiah do in the sight of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:2 (ESV): "And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done."

questions.question: Against whom did Zedekiah rebel, bringing upon Jerusalem the wrath of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:3 (ESV): "And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon."

questions.question: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, what did Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon do?
options: He came with all his army against Jerusalem and laid siege to it
questions.correctAnswer: He came with all his army against Jerusalem and laid siege to it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:4 (ESV): "And in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem, and laid siege to it."

questions.question: By the fourth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, what severe condition existed in the city?
options: The famine was so severe that there was no food for the people of the land
questions.correctAnswer: The famine was so severe that there was no food for the people of the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:6 (ESV): "the famine was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land."

questions.question: When a breach was made in the city, the king and all the men of war fled by night. Where did they intend to go?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:7 (ESV): "Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night... And they went in the direction of the Arabah."

questions.question: Where did the Chaldean army overtake Zedekiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:8 (ESV): "But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho,"

questions.question: What was the physical punishment inflicted upon Zedekiah by the king of Babylon?
options: His sons were killed before him, and then his eyes were put out
He was starved to death in a cistern
His hands and feet were cut off
questions.correctAnswer: His sons were killed before him, and then his eyes were put out
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:10-11 (ESV): "The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes... He put out the eyes of Zedekiah..."

questions.question: Who came to Jerusalem and burned the house of the Lord, the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem?
options: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the bodyguard
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the bodyguard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:12-13 (ESV): "Nebuzaradan, the captain of the bodyguard... came to Jerusalem. And he burned the house of the Lord, and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem;"

questions.question: What did the Chaldeans break into pieces and carry to Babylon from the temple?
options: The bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze sea
questions.correctAnswer: The bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze sea
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:17 (ESV): "And the pillars of bronze that were in the house of the Lord, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the Lord, the Chaldeans broke in pieces, and carried all the bronze of them to Babylon."

questions.question: Who was the chief priest that Nebuzaradan took captive and brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:24 (ESV): "And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold;"

questions.question: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, what did Evil-merodach king of Babylon do?
options: He graciously freed Jehoiachin from prison
He destroyed the rest of Jerusalem
He sent Jehoiachin back to rule Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He graciously freed Jehoiachin from prison
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:31 (ESV): "Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison."

questions.question: How did Evil-merodach speak to Jehoiachin?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:32 (ESV): "And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon."

questions.question: What did Jehoiachin do for the rest of his life after being freed?
options: He dined regularly at the king's table
He worked in the fields of Babylon
He lived in a tent outside the city
questions.correctAnswer: He dined regularly at the king's table
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:33 (ESV): "So Jehoiachin put off his prison garments. And every day of his life he dined regularly at the king's table."

questions.question: Did Jehoiachin receive an allowance?
options: Yes, a regular daily allowance was given him by the king according to his daily needs, until the day of his death.
No, he lived off the charity of other exiles.
Yes, he was given one talent of silver per year.
No, he was expected to pay for his own food.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, a regular daily allowance was given him by the king according to his daily needs, until the day of his death.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52:34 (ESV): "and for his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king of Babylon according to his daily needs, until the day of his death, as long as he lived."

key_verse_text: And in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah... Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison. And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
